- `scripts/promote.sh` — promotes exact commit from dev to production

# Deploy Skill — FibreFlow Deployment Procedures

## Overview

Full deployment reference for FibreFlow dev and production environments on Velocity.
Covers standard deploys, promotions, rollbacks, health verification, log tailing, and emergency recovery.

---

## Quick Reference

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Dev URL | https://dev.fibreflow.app |
| Production URL | https://app.fibreflow.app |
| Dev service | `fibreflow-dev.service` (port 3005) |
| Production service | `fibreflow-production.service` (port 3000) |
| Dev deploy dir | `/home/velo/fibreflow-dev` |
| Production deploy dir | `/home/velo/fibreflow-production` |
| Recommended deploy script | `scripts/deploy-local.sh` |
| Rollback script | `scripts/rollback.sh` |
| Smoke test script | `scripts/post-deploy-smoke.sh` |

---

## Deployment Rules (MANDATORY)

| Time Window | Dev | Production |
|-------------|-----|------------|
| Business hours (08:00-17:00 SAST, Mon-Fri) | Allowed | BLOCKED |
| After hours + weekends | Allowed | Allowed (Hein approval required) |
| Emergency (any time) | Allowed | `--force` + Hein confirmation |

**Hein's approval is required for ALL production deployments without exception.**

---

## Standard Deploy Commands

We run directly on Velocity — no SSH to self. Use `deploy-local.sh` (preferred over `deploy-gate.sh`).

```bash
# Deploy to dev (always allowed)
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh dev

# Deploy to dev on a specific branch
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh dev --branch fix/my-branch

# Check deployment status (shows commit + service state for all envs)
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh status

# Promote exact dev commit to production (after hours only)
bash scripts/promote.sh dev production

# Emergency production deploy (requires typing 'EMERGENCY' to confirm)
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh production --force
```

What `deploy-local.sh` does automatically:
1. Fixes `.next` ownership (prevents EACCES from mixed hein/velo/root builds)
2. Stops the service before building (prevents crash-loop interference)
3. Backs up existing `.next` to `.next-backup-TIMESTAMP`
4. Retries build up to 3 times (handles Next.js 14 race condition)
5. Validates BUILD_ID after build
6. Starts service + HTTP health check
7. Keeps last 3 `.next-backup-*` builds for rollback

---

## Post-Deploy Health Verification

Run immediately after every deploy to confirm the app is healthy.

```bash
# Full smoke test suite (checks HTTP + content + JSON validity)
bash scripts/post-deploy-smoke.sh dev
bash scripts/post-deploy-smoke.sh production

# Quick manual checks — dev
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://dev.fibreflow.app/sign-in
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://dev.fibreflow.app/api/health
curl -s --max-time 5 https://dev.fibreflow.app/api/health | python3 -m json.tool

# Quick manual checks — production
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://app.fibreflow.app/sign-in
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://app.fibreflow.app/api/health
curl -s --max-time 5 https://app.fibreflow.app/api/health | python3 -m json.tool

# Local port checks (bypasses Cloudflare — definitive test)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:3005/sign-in   # dev
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:3000/sign-in   # production

# Verify which commit is running
sudo -u velo bash -c 'cd /home/velo/fibreflow-dev && git log -1 --oneline'
sudo -u velo bash -c 'cd /home/velo/fibreflow-production && git log -1 --oneline'

# Check BUILD_ID matches what was built
sudo -u velo cat /home/velo/fibreflow-dev/.next/BUILD_ID
sudo -u velo cat /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/BUILD_ID
```

The smoke test (`post-deploy-smoke.sh`) checks:
- Service responding on local port within 60s
- Sign-in page returns HTTP 200 (public URL)
- Root URL redirect (HTTP 200)
- `/api/health` returns HTTP 200
- Sign-in page contains expected content (not a blank/error page)
- `/api/health` returns valid JSON

---

## Log Tailing

Check service logs immediately after deploy to catch startup errors.

```bash
# Live log tail — dev (follow mode, Ctrl+C to stop)
journalctl -u fibreflow-dev -f

# Live log tail — production
journalctl -u fibreflow-production -f

# Last 100 lines — dev
journalctl -u fibreflow-dev -n 100

# Last 100 lines — production
journalctl -u fibreflow-production -n 100

# Last 50 lines with timestamps — production (useful after restart)
journalctl -u fibreflow-production -n 50 --no-pager

# Logs since last restart (isolates this boot's logs)
journalctl -u fibreflow-production -b

# Filter for errors only
journalctl -u fibreflow-production -n 200 --no-pager | grep -i "error\|fail\|crash"

# Deploy history log (tracks all deploys + rollbacks)
tail -20 /home/velo/fibreflow-production/logs/deploy-history.log
tail -20 /home/velo/fibreflow-dev/logs/deploy-history.log

# Service status (shows last exit code + recent log snippet)
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-dev.service
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-production.service
```

---

## Rollback Procedures

Three rollback methods — choose based on severity.

### Method 1: Build Backup Restore (fastest — no rebuild needed)

The deploy script keeps the last 3 `.next-backup-TIMESTAMP` directories.
This restores the previous working build in ~30 seconds without a rebuild.

```bash
# Production rollback (interactive — prompts for confirmation)
sudo -u velo bash /home/hein/Workspace/FF_Next.js/scripts/rollback.sh

# Manual build backup restore (dev)
sudo -u velo bash -c '
  cd /home/velo/fibreflow-dev
  LATEST=$(ls -t .next-backup-* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  echo "Restoring: $LATEST"
  mv .next .next-failed-$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
  cp -r "$LATEST" .next
'
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-dev.service

# List available backups to pick a specific one
sudo -u velo bash -c 'ls -lt /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next-backup-* 2>/dev/null | head -5'
```

### Method 2: Git Revert to Previous Commit (rebuild required)

Use when you need to revert a specific bad commit (not just the build artifact).

```bash
# Find the commit to revert to
sudo -u velo bash -c 'cd /home/velo/fibreflow-production && git log --oneline -10'

# Roll back to a specific commit (replace SHA with actual commit hash)
sudo -u velo bash -c 'cd /home/velo/fibreflow-production && git checkout <PREVIOUS_COMMIT_SHA>'

# Rebuild and restart
sudo -u velo bash -c 'cd /home/velo/fibreflow-production && npm run build'
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-production.service

# Verify rollback
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://app.fibreflow.app/sign-in
```

### Method 3: Git Revert PR (safest — creates a revert commit on master)

Use for planned rollbacks where you want a clean audit trail on master.

```bash
# In the local workspace, create a revert commit
git revert <BAD_COMMIT_SHA> --no-edit
git push origin fix/revert-bad-deploy

# Open a PR, merge, then redeploy
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh production
```

---

## Common Deploy Failures and Fixes

### Build Error: TypeScript / ESLint

**Symptom:** `npm run build` exits with type errors or lint errors.

**Diagnosis:**
```bash
sudo -u velo bash -c 'cd /home/velo/fibreflow-dev && npm run build 2>&1 | tail -60'
```

**Fix:** Fix errors in local workspace, push to master, redeploy.
```bash
npm run type-check   # in local workspace (/home/hein/Workspace/FF_Next.js)
npm run lint
```

**Never fix TypeScript errors directly in deploy directories** — those are deploy targets, not workspaces.

---

### Build Error: Out of Memory

**Symptom:** Build kills mid-way with no error message, or `Killed` output.

**Diagnosis:**
```bash
free -h   # Check available RAM
dmesg | tail -20 | grep -i "oom\|killed"
```

**Fix:** Close other heavy processes (VLM inference jobs, etc.) and retry.
```bash
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh dev   # retries build up to 3 times automatically
```

---

### Build Error: Stale `.next` Artifacts (Next.js Race Condition)

**Symptom:** Build fails with `ENOENT rename .next/...` or `unlink .next/...` errors.

**Fix:** `deploy-local.sh` handles this automatically with up to 3 retries and artifact cleanup. If using manual commands:
```bash
sudo -u velo bash -c 'rm -rf /home/velo/fibreflow-dev/.next'
sudo -u velo bash -c 'cd /home/velo/fibreflow-dev && npm run build'
```

---

### Permission Error: EACCES on `.next`

**Symptom:** `Error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '.next/...'` during build.

**Root cause:** Previous build ran as `root` or `hein`, leaving files owned by the wrong user. The velo process cannot write over them.

**Fix:** Use the privileged helper script (NOPASSWD in sudoers):
```bash
sudo /usr/local/bin/fibreflow-fix-next /home/velo/fibreflow-dev
sudo /usr/local/bin/fibreflow-fix-next /home/velo/fibreflow-production
```

**Fallback if helper not available:**
```bash
sudo chown -R velo:velo /home/velo/fibreflow-dev/.next
sudo chown -R velo:velo /home/velo/fibreflow-dev/.git
```

---

### Port Already in Use

**Symptom:** Service fails to start; logs show `EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3005`.

**Diagnosis:**
```bash
ss -tlnp | grep ':3005'   # dev
ss -tlnp | grep ':3000'   # production
lsof -i :3005
```

**Fix:** Find and stop only the conflicting process — do NOT use broad pkill.
```bash
# Identify the exact PID
lsof -i :3005
# Then kill only that specific PID (replace 12345 with actual PID)
kill 12345
# Restart the service
sudo systemctl start fibreflow-dev.service
```

---

### Git Permission Denied

**Symptom:** `error: cannot open '.git/FETCH_HEAD': Permission denied`

**Fix:**
```bash
sudo chown -R velo:velo /home/velo/fibreflow-dev/.git
sudo chown -R velo:velo /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.git
```

---

**Symptom:** `deploy-local.sh` reports service not active; `systemctl status` shows `failed`.

**Diagnosis sequence:**
```bash
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-production.service
journalctl -u fibreflow-production -n 50 --no-pager
# Look for: missing env vars, port conflicts, build errors
```

**Common causes:**
1. Missing `.env.local` or `.env.production` variables — check env file exists and has correct values
2. Port conflict — see "Port Already in Use" above
3. Corrupted build — run rollback (Method 1 above), then redeploy after fixing the issue

**Symptom:** Browser shows 502; service is active but unreachable externally.

**Diagnosis:**

---

## Incident Runbooks

Step-by-step resolution procedures for the five most common FibreFlow incidents. Each runbook follows the Diagnose → Fix → Guard → Verify pattern.

---

### Runbook 1: 502 Bad Gateway (nginx → app not running)

**Symptom:** `https://app.fibreflow.app` or `https://dev.fibreflow.app` returns a 502 or shows the branded maintenance page.

**Health endpoints to check first:**
```bash
# Quick status — all environments
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/health | jq '.status'   # production
curl -s http://localhost:3005/api/health | jq '.status'   # dev

# Systemd service status
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-production.service
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-dev.service
```

**Step 1 — Identify which layer is broken:**
```bash
# Is the app process even listening?
ss -tlnp | grep -E '300[05]'

# Check nginx config (should be direct proxy_pass, no upstream blocks)
sudo nginx -t
grep -A3 'proxy_pass' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/vf-fibreflow

# Check systemd failure reason
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "30 min ago" | tail -50
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "30 min ago" | tail -50
```

**Step 2 — Check for crash-loop or build corruption:**
```bash
# Look for restart count (high = crash-loop)
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-production.service | grep -E '(Active|restarts)'

# Check if .next/BUILD_ID exists and is owned correctly
ls -la /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/BUILD_ID
stat /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/

# If .next is missing or owned by root, the build is corrupted
sudo ls /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/ | head -5
```

**Step 3 — Standard recovery (try in order):**
```bash
# Option A: Simple restart (works for transient crashes)
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-production.service
sleep 10 && curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/health | jq '.status'

# Option B: Fix ownership + restart (works for mixed-user file issues)
sudo /usr/local/bin/fibreflow-fix-next /home/velo/fibreflow-production
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-production.service

# Option C: Full redeploy (works for corrupted .next)
bash /home/hein/Workspace/FF_Next.js/scripts/deploy-local.sh production --force
```

**Step 4 — Verify nginx is not stuck on dead upstream:**
```bash
# Check current nginx config — should NOT have upstream blocks
grep -n 'upstream\|proxy_pass' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/vf-fibreflow

# If upstream blocks exist with VPS IPs (72.61.197.178), this is the old bug
# Fix: replace with direct proxy_pass http://localhost:<port>
sudo nginx -s reload
```

**Step 5 — Check for duplicate services on same port:**
```bash
# Port conflict check
sudo systemctl list-units --type=service | grep fibreflow
ss -tlnp | grep -E 'LISTEN.*300[056]'
```

**Auto-recovery:** The health check script `/home/velo/scripts/fibreflow-health-check-v2.sh` runs every 5 minutes and auto-restarts services returning non-200. Check its log if the 502 is recurring:
```bash
tail -50 /var/log/fibreflow-health.log
```

**Escalate to Hein if:** Service restarts more than 5 times within 10 minutes, or `.next` is corrupted by an agent commit (check git reflog for "Jarvis", "Flow", "Forge" authors in deploy dirs).

---

### Runbook 2: Neon Database Timeout (error code 1033)

**Symptom:** API returns HTTP 530 or 500 with `"error code: 1033"`. Bridge logs show `[ACK WARN] Acknowledgment API returned 530 for DRXXXXXX: error code: 1033`. Dashboard shows loading spinners that never resolve.

**Context:** Error 1033 is a Neon-specific code for a connection pool timeout or cold-start delay (Neon serverless branches can hibernate). It is almost always transient.

**Step 1 — Confirm it is Neon, not the app:**
```bash
# Test the health endpoint — it runs a SELECT 1
curl -s https://app.fibreflow.app/api/health | jq '.checks.database'
# Expected: "connected" with latency
# If "error": the DB connection is broken

# Check detailed system health (requires admin session)
curl -s 'https://app.fibreflow.app/api/system/health' | jq '.services[] | select(.name | test("database|neon"; "i"))'
```

**Step 2 — Check Neon endpoint directly:**
```bash
# Quick DB ping from Velocity (uses env from local dev)
cd /home/hein/Workspace/FF_Next.js
node -e "
const { neon } = require('@neondatabase/serverless');
const sql = neon(process.env.DATABASE_URL || process.env.DIRECT_URL);
sql\`SELECT 1 as ok, current_timestamp\`.then(r => console.log('OK', r)).catch(e => console.error('FAIL', e.message));
"
```

**Step 3 — Wait and retry (most common fix):**
- Neon cold-start timeouts typically resolve within 30-60 seconds.
- Do NOT restart the app service — the problem is upstream of the app.
- Wait 60 seconds, then re-check `/api/health`.

**Step 4 — If sustained (>5 minutes):**
```bash
# Check Neon status page
curl -s https://neonstatus.com/api/v2/status.json | jq '.status.description'

# Check for connection pool exhaustion in app logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "10 min ago" | grep -i 'neon\|pool\|connection\|1033\|530'
```

**Step 5 — For bridge ack failures (error 1033 in bridge log):**
The bridge has a 3-layer retry + local ACK fallback. It will self-heal in most cases. To verify:
```bash
ssh root@72.61.197.178 "tail -50 /opt/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.log | grep -E '(ACK RETRY|ACK FAILED|LOCAL ACK|ACK FALLBACK)'"
```
If `[ACK FAILED]` appears after 3 retries, send the ACK manually — see Runbook 4.

**Escalate to Hein if:** Timeout lasts longer than 15 minutes, or query errors appear in Neon console (corrupted data, not just timeouts).

**Known anti-pattern:** Never use conditional SQL fragments (`${cond ? sql\`AND x\` : sql\`\`}`) — these crash the Neon driver. If a timeout appears on a specific query after a code change, check for this pattern.

---

### Runbook 3: VLM Service Down (GPU/model issues)

**Symptom:** Photo categorization fails in the Activate module, fleet VLM plate reads return errors, or `/api/noc/devops-vlm-analyse` returns 500/503.

**Service:** `vllm-qwen.service` on Velocity (100.96.203.105), serving on port 8100.

**Step 1 — Health check:**
```bash
curl -s http://100.96.203.105:8100/health
# Expected: HTTP 200 with model info
# If connection refused: service is down
# If HTTP 400 with "decoder prompt is longer": image too large (not a service failure)
```

**Step 2 — Check service status and GPU:**
```bash
sudo systemctl status vllm-qwen.service
nvidia-smi                              # Check GPU utilization and memory
sudo journalctl -u vllm-qwen.service -n 50
```

**Step 3 — Identify failure mode:**

| Log pattern | Cause | Fix |
|-------------|-------|-----|
| `CUDA out of memory` | GPU OOM | Restart service; reduce `--max-num-seqs` if recurring |
| `FLASHINFER` crash | Missing `--enforce-eager` flag | Check service config, restart |
| `Model not found` | Model weights missing | Check `/home/velo/.cache/huggingface/` |
| Connection refused | Service not started | Start with startup script |
| `decoder prompt is longer` | Image exceeds 16384 tokens | Resize to 1024x768 max — not a service failure |

**Step 4 — Standard restart:**
```bash
# Use the managed startup script (handles GPU wait, model load)
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh

# Verify it came up (model load takes ~60-120 seconds)
sleep 90 && curl -s http://100.96.203.105:8100/health
```

**Step 5 — Verify with benchmark:**
```bash
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmark.sh
cat /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmarks/latest_results.json | jq '.results[] | {test, passed, time_ms}'
```

**Step 6 — Check maintenance logs:**
```bash
tail -30 /var/log/vllm-benchmark.log
tail -30 /var/log/vllm-maintenance.log
```

**Escalate to Hein if:** GPU shows errors in `nvidia-smi` (not just high utilization), model weights are missing or corrupt, or the service crashes within 5 minutes of restart (loop).

**Note:** VLM restarts every night at 03:00 via cron and runs benchmarks at 06:00, 12:00, 18:00, 23:00. A failure detected between 03:00-04:00 is likely the nightly restart — check cron logs before alarming.

---

### Runbook 4: WhatsApp Bridge Disconnected

**Symptom:** DR acknowledgments not being sent, technicians not receiving confirmations, bridge health returns disconnected status, or bridge logs show `[DISCONNECTED]` or QR code prompts.

**Service:** `whatsapp-bridge` on VPS 72.61.197.178, port 8083.

**Step 1 — Health check:**
```bash
curl -s http://72.61.197.178:8083/health | jq '.'
# Look for: "status": "connected" and phone number present
```

**Step 2 — Check bridge logs:**
```bash
ssh root@72.61.197.178 "tail -100 /opt/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.log"

# Key patterns to grep for:
ssh root@72.61.197.178 "tail -200 /opt/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.log | grep -E '(DISCONNECTED|QR|401|FAILED|WebSocket EOF|session)'"
```

**Step 3 — Service status:**
```bash
ssh root@72.61.197.178 "systemctl status whatsapp-bridge"
```

**Step 4 — Standard restart (handles transient disconnects):**
```bash
ssh root@72.61.197.178 "systemctl restart whatsapp-bridge"
sleep 15
curl -s http://72.61.197.178:8083/health | jq '.status'
```

**Step 5 — If QR code is showing (session expired):**
The bridge phone (+27 63 841 2276) needs re-pairing. This requires physical phone access — escalate to Hein immediately. Do not attempt to re-pair automatically.

**Step 6 — Send manual ACK for any DRs that failed during outage:**
```bash
# Find DRs that failed to get an ACK (submitted in last 2 hours, no ack_sent)
# Then manually send each one:
ACK_DATA=$(curl -s -X POST "https://app.fibreflow.app/api/activate/dr-acknowledgment" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

    \"group_jid\": \"120363418298130331@g.us\",

**Step 7 — Verify wa-feedback proxy on Velocity is also healthy:**

sudo systemctl status wa-feedback

**Escalate to Hein if:** QR code is required (phone session expired), WebSocket EOF errors return after restart (suggests another service is using the same WhatsApp session), or bridge binary needs replacement.

### Runbook 5: High Memory / CPU on Velocity

**Symptom:** Application responses slow, VLM inference timing out, `top` or `htop` shows very high CPU/RAM consumption, or `/api/health` reports `memory: "high"` or `memory: "critical"`.

**Memory thresholds in `/api/health`:**
- `ok` = heap < 500 MB
- `high` = heap 500-800 MB (status: `degraded`)
- `critical` = heap > 800 MB (status: `unhealthy`, HTTP 503)

**Step 1 — Identify the resource consumer:**
```bash
# Overall system view
top -b -n1 | head -25

# Per-process memory
ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -20

# Per-process CPU
ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head -20

# Node.js heap from health API
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/health | jq '.details.memory'
curl -s http://localhost:3005/api/health | jq '.details.memory'
```

**Step 2 — Common culprits and fixes:**

| Process | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `node` (fibreflow-production) | Memory leak after long uptime | `sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-production.service` |
| `node` (fibreflow-dev) | Memory leak | `sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-dev.service` |
| `python` (vllm-qwen) | GPU+CPU RAM during inference | Restart VLM: `/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh` |
| `python` (ai-recovery-agent) | Runaway health check loop | `sudo systemctl restart ai-recovery-agent.service` |
| `node` (qfield-sync) | Stuck sync job | `sudo systemctl restart qfield-sync` |

**Step 3 — Check for memory leak patterns in app logs:**
```bash
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "2 hours ago" | grep -iE '(OOM|heap|memory|ENOMEM|killed)'

# Check system OOM killer
sudo dmesg | grep -i 'oom\|killed process' | tail -20
```

**Step 4 — Disk space (often causes swap pressure):**
```bash
df -h
du -sh /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next-backup-* 2>/dev/null | sort -h
# Remove old backups if disk is full (keep latest 3)
```

**Step 5 — GPU memory (VLM-specific):**
```bash
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free,utilization.gpu --format=csv
# If memory.used is near max and utilization is 0 = GPU memory leak
# Fix: restart vllm-qwen.service
```

**Step 6 — Scheduled maintenance (if nothing is actively crashing):**
The VLM service restarts nightly at 03:00 — this reclaims GPU memory. For Node.js, a weekly rolling restart is the safest approach; raise this with Hein if it becomes recurring.

**Escalate to Hein if:** OOM killer has terminated a service, disk usage is above 85%, or CPU stays above 95% for more than 10 minutes with no obvious cause.

### Escalate to Hein (do not attempt to resolve)

| Situation | Why | How to notify |
|-----------|-----|---------------|

| Production 502 lasting >15 minutes | SLA breach, customer impact | WhatsApp + update ticket as critical |

| Auth/security vulnerability found | Credential leak, permission bypass | Direct message to Hein immediately |

## Incident Runbooks

Step-by-step resolution procedures for the five most common FibreFlow incidents. Each runbook follows the Diagnose → Fix → Guard → Verify pattern.

---

### Runbook 1: 502 Bad Gateway (nginx → app not running)

**Symptom:** `https://app.fibreflow.app` or `https://dev.fibreflow.app` returns a 502 or shows the branded maintenance page.

**Health endpoints to check first:**
```bash
# Quick status — all environments
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/health | jq '.status'   # production
curl -s http://localhost:3005/api/health | jq '.status'   # dev

# Systemd service status
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-production.service
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-dev.service
```

**Step 1 — Identify which layer is broken:**
```bash
# Is the app process even listening?
ss -tlnp | grep -E '300[05]'

# Check nginx config (should be direct proxy_pass, no upstream blocks)
sudo nginx -t
grep -A3 'proxy_pass' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/vf-fibreflow

# Check systemd failure reason
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "30 min ago" | tail -50
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "30 min ago" | tail -50
```

**Step 2 — Check for crash-loop or build corruption:**
```bash
# Look for restart count (high = crash-loop)
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-production.service | grep -E '(Active|restarts)'

# Check if .next/BUILD_ID exists and is owned correctly
ls -la /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/BUILD_ID
stat /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/

# If .next is missing or owned by root, the build is corrupted
sudo ls /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/ | head -5
```

**Step 3 — Standard recovery (try in order):**
```bash
# Option A: Simple restart (works for transient crashes)
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-production.service
sleep 10 && curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/health | jq '.status'

# Option B: Fix ownership + restart (works for mixed-user file issues)
sudo /usr/local/bin/fibreflow-fix-next /home/velo/fibreflow-production
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-production.service

# Option C: Full redeploy (works for corrupted .next)
bash /home/hein/Workspace/FF_Next.js/scripts/deploy-local.sh production --force
```

**Step 4 — Verify nginx is not stuck on dead upstream:**
```bash
# Check current nginx config — should NOT have upstream blocks
grep -n 'upstream\|proxy_pass' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/vf-fibreflow

# If upstream blocks exist with VPS IPs (72.61.197.178), this is the old bug
# Fix: replace with direct proxy_pass http://localhost:<port>
sudo nginx -s reload
```

**Step 5 — Check for duplicate services on same port:**
```bash
# Port conflict check
sudo systemctl list-units --type=service | grep fibreflow
ss -tlnp | grep -E 'LISTEN.*300[056]'
```

**Auto-recovery:** The health check script `/home/velo/scripts/fibreflow-health-check-v2.sh` runs every 5 minutes and auto-restarts services returning non-200. Check its log if the 502 is recurring:
```bash
tail -50 /var/log/fibreflow-health.log
```

**Escalate to Hein if:** Service restarts more than 5 times within 10 minutes, or `.next` is corrupted by an agent commit (check git reflog for "Jarvis", "Flow", "Forge" authors in deploy dirs).

---

### Runbook 2: Neon Database Timeout (error code 1033)

**Symptom:** API returns HTTP 530 or 500 with `"error code: 1033"`. Bridge logs show `[ACK WARN] Acknowledgment API returned 530 for DRXXXXXX: error code: 1033`. Dashboard shows loading spinners that never resolve.

**Context:** Error 1033 is a Neon-specific code for a connection pool timeout or cold-start delay (Neon serverless branches can hibernate). It is almost always transient.

**Step 1 — Confirm it is Neon, not the app:**
```bash
# Test the health endpoint — it runs a SELECT 1
curl -s https://app.fibreflow.app/api/health | jq '.checks.database'
# Expected: "connected" with latency
# If "error": the DB connection is broken

# Check detailed system health (requires admin session)
curl -s 'https://app.fibreflow.app/api/system/health' | jq '.services[] | select(.name | test("database|neon"; "i"))'
```

**Step 2 — Check Neon endpoint directly:**
```bash
# Quick DB ping from Velocity (uses env from local dev)
cd /home/hein/Workspace/FF_Next.js
node -e "
const { neon } = require('@neondatabase/serverless');
const sql = neon(process.env.DATABASE_URL || process.env.DIRECT_URL);
sql\`SELECT 1 as ok, current_timestamp\`.then(r => console.log('OK', r)).catch(e => console.error('FAIL', e.message));
"
```

**Step 3 — Wait and retry (most common fix):**
- Neon cold-start timeouts typically resolve within 30-60 seconds.
- Do NOT restart the app service — the problem is upstream of the app.
- Wait 60 seconds, then re-check `/api/health`.

**Step 4 — If sustained (>5 minutes):**
```bash
# Check Neon status page
curl -s https://neonstatus.com/api/v2/status.json | jq '.status.description'

# Check for connection pool exhaustion in app logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "10 min ago" | grep -i 'neon\|pool\|connection\|1033\|530'
```

**Step 5 — For bridge ack failures (error 1033 in bridge log):**
The bridge has a 3-layer retry + local ACK fallback. It will self-heal in most cases. To verify:
```bash
ssh root@72.61.197.178 "tail -50 /opt/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.log | grep -E '(ACK RETRY|ACK FAILED|LOCAL ACK|ACK FALLBACK)'"
```
If `[ACK FAILED]` appears after 3 retries, send the ACK manually — see Runbook 4.

**Escalate to Hein if:** Timeout lasts longer than 15 minutes, or query errors appear in Neon console (corrupted data, not just timeouts).

**Known anti-pattern:** Never use conditional SQL fragments (`${cond ? sql\`AND x\` : sql\`\`}`) — these crash the Neon driver. If a timeout appears on a specific query after a code change, check for this pattern.

### Runbook 3: VLM Service Down (GPU/model issues)

| `FLASHINFER` crash | Missing `--enforce-eager` flag | Check service config, restart |

## Incident Runbooks

Step-by-step resolution procedures for the five most common FibreFlow incidents. Each runbook follows the Diagnose → Fix → Guard → Verify pattern.

### Runbook 1: 502 Bad Gateway (nginx → app not running)

**Symptom:** `https://app.fibreflow.app` or `https://dev.fibreflow.app` returns a 502 or shows the branded maintenance page.

**Health endpoints to check first:**
```bash
# Quick status — all environments
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/health | jq '.status'   # production
curl -s http://localhost:3005/api/health | jq '.status'   # dev

# Systemd service status
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-production.service
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-dev.service
```

**Step 1 — Identify which layer is broken:**
```bash
# Is the app process even listening?
ss -tlnp | grep -E '300[05]'

# Check nginx config (should be direct proxy_pass, no upstream blocks)
sudo nginx -t
grep -A3 'proxy_pass' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/vf-fibreflow

# Check systemd failure reason
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "30 min ago" | tail -50
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "30 min ago" | tail -50
```

**Step 2 — Check for crash-loop or build corruption:**
```bash
# Look for restart count (high = crash-loop)
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-production.service | grep -E '(Active|restarts)'

# Check if .next/BUILD_ID exists and is owned correctly
ls -la /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/BUILD_ID
stat /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/

# If .next is missing or owned by root, the build is corrupted
sudo ls /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/ | head -5
```

**Step 3 — Standard recovery (try in order):**
```bash
# Option A: Simple restart (works for transient crashes)
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-production.service
sleep 10 && curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/health | jq '.status'

# Option B: Fix ownership + restart (works for mixed-user file issues)
sudo /usr/local/bin/fibreflow-fix-next /home/velo/fibreflow-production
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-production.service

# Option C: Full redeploy (works for corrupted .next)
bash /home/hein/Workspace/FF_Next.js/scripts/deploy-local.sh production --force
```

**Step 4 — Verify nginx is not stuck on dead upstream:**
```bash
# Check current nginx config — should NOT have upstream blocks
grep -n 'upstream\|proxy_pass' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/vf-fibreflow

# If upstream blocks exist with VPS IPs (72.61.197.178), this is the old bug
# Fix: replace with direct proxy_pass http://localhost:<port>
sudo nginx -s reload
```

**Step 5 — Check for duplicate services on same port:**
```bash
# Port conflict check
sudo systemctl list-units --type=service | grep fibreflow
ss -tlnp | grep -E 'LISTEN.*300[056]'
```

**Auto-recovery:** The health check script `/home/velo/scripts/fibreflow-health-check-v2.sh` runs every 5 minutes and auto-restarts services returning non-200. Check its log if the 502 is recurring:
```bash
tail -50 /var/log/fibreflow-health.log
```

**Escalate to Hein if:** Service restarts more than 5 times within 10 minutes, or `.next` is corrupted by an agent commit (check git reflog for "Jarvis", "Flow", "Forge" authors in deploy dirs).

### Runbook 2: Neon Database Timeout (error code 1033)

**Symptom:** API returns HTTP 530 or 500 with `"error code: 1033"`. Bridge logs show `[ACK WARN] Acknowledgment API returned 530 for DRXXXXXX: error code: 1033`. Dashboard shows loading spinners that never resolve.

**Context:** Error 1033 is a Neon-specific code for a connection pool timeout or cold-start delay (Neon serverless branches can hibernate). It is almost always transient.

**Step 1 — Confirm it is Neon, not the app:**
```bash
# Test the health endpoint — it runs a SELECT 1
curl -s https://app.fibreflow.app/api/health | jq '.checks.database'
# Expected: "connected" with latency
# If "error": the DB connection is broken

# Check detailed system health (requires admin session)
curl -s 'https://app.fibreflow.app/api/system/health' | jq '.services[] | select(.name | test("database|neon"; "i"))'
```

**Step 2 — Check Neon endpoint directly:**
```bash
# Quick DB ping from Velocity (uses env from local dev)
cd /home/hein/Workspace/FF_Next.js
node -e "
const { neon } = require('@neondatabase/serverless');
const sql = neon(process.env.DATABASE_URL || process.env.DIRECT_URL);
sql\`SELECT 1 as ok, current_timestamp\`.then(r => console.log('OK', r)).catch(e => console.error('FAIL', e.message));
"
```

**Step 3 — Wait and retry (most common fix):**
- Neon cold-start timeouts typically resolve within 30-60 seconds.
- Do NOT restart the app service — the problem is upstream of the app.
- Wait 60 seconds, then re-check `/api/health`.

**Step 4 — If sustained (>5 minutes):**
```bash
# Check Neon status page
curl -s https://neonstatus.com/api/v2/status.json | jq '.status.description'

# Check for connection pool exhaustion in app logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "10 min ago" | grep -i 'neon\|pool\|connection\|1033\|530'
```

**Step 5 — For bridge ack failures (error 1033 in bridge log):**
The bridge has a 3-layer retry + local ACK fallback. It will self-heal in most cases. To verify:
```bash
ssh root@72.61.197.178 "tail -50 /opt/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.log | grep -E '(ACK RETRY|ACK FAILED|LOCAL ACK|ACK FALLBACK)'"
```
If `[ACK FAILED]` appears after 3 retries, send the ACK manually — see Runbook 4.

**Escalate to Hein if:** Timeout lasts longer than 15 minutes, or query errors appear in Neon console (corrupted data, not just timeouts).

**Known anti-pattern:** Never use conditional SQL fragments (`${cond ? sql\`AND x\` : sql\`\`}`) — these crash the Neon driver. If a timeout appears on a specific query after a code change, check for this pattern.

### Auto-Resolve (no escalation needed)

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|

| QField sync stale | `sudo systemctl restart qfield-sync` |
| AI recovery agent stuck | `sudo systemctl restart ai-recovery-agent.service` |

| Nginx config change required | Affects all environments | Submit PR, wait for Hein review |
| Service cost > $50 (Neon egress, etc.) | Budget impact | Flag in ticket |
| Unknown recurring crash (>5 restarts) | Root cause unclear | Escalate with full logs attached |

# /noc — NOC Tickets

Autonomous agent that picks up tickets from the NOC queue, triages by priority/SLA, diagnoses issues using the codebase, logs, and existing skills, implements fixes via PR workflow, deploys, verifies with screenshots, and resolves tickets with proof attached.

## Quick Reference

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| **Ticket table** | `maintenance_tickets` (type = `dev_ops`) |
| **Extension table** | `dev_ticket_details` (error_url, stack_trace, affected_module, etc.) |
| **Ticket UID format** | `VF-YYYYMMDD-NNN` |
| **API — list tickets** | `GET /api/noc/tickets?ticket_type=dev_ops&status=open,assigned` |
| **API — ticket detail** | `GET /api/noc/tickets/[id]` |
| **API — update ticket** | `PUT /api/noc/tickets/[id]` |
| **API — verification steps** | `GET/PUT /api/noc/tickets/[id]/verification/[step]` |
| **API — VLM screenshot** | `POST /api/noc/devops-vlm-analyse` |
| **Dev URL** | `https://dev.fibreflow.app` (port 3005) |
| **Prod URL** | `https://app.fibreflow.app` (port 3000) |
| **Local URL** | `http://localhost:3004` |

## Agent Workflow

When triggered, follow this sequence:

### Phase 1: Ticket Intake

```bash
# 1. Fetch open/assigned DevOps tickets
curl -s "http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets?ticket_type=dev_ops&status=open,assigned&limit=20" \
  -H "Cookie: $(cat .claude/credentials.local.md | grep SESSION | cut -d'=' -f2)" | jq '.data'
```

Or query the database directly:

```sql
-- Open DevOps tickets with details
SELECT
  t.id, t.ticket_uid, t.title, t.status, t.priority,
  t.created_at, t.assigned_to,
  d.affected_module, d.environment, d.error_url,
  d.stack_trace, d.steps_to_reproduce, d.browser_info,
  d.agent_status
FROM maintenance_tickets t
LEFT JOIN dev_ticket_details d ON d.ticket_id = t.id
WHERE t.ticket_type = 'dev_ops'
  AND t.status IN ('open', 'assigned', 'in_progress')
ORDER BY
  CASE t.priority
    WHEN 'critical' THEN 1
    WHEN 'urgent' THEN 2
    WHEN 'high' THEN 3
    WHEN 'normal' THEN 4
    WHEN 'low' THEN 5
  END,
  t.created_at ASC;
```

### Phase 2: Triage & Prioritize

For each ticket, assess:

1. **Severity** — Is production affected? How many users impacted?
2. **Module** — Which FibreFlow module? (Dashboard, NOC, Activate, Procurement, etc.)
3. **Reproducibility** — Can we reproduce from steps_to_reproduce?
4. **Quick win?** — Is it a known pattern (see Common Patterns below)?

**Priority matrix:**
| Priority | SLA | Action |
|----------|-----|--------|
| Critical | 6h | Drop everything, fix immediately |
| Urgent | 12h | Fix within session |
| High | 1d | Fix today |
| Normal | 3d | Queue for next session |
| Low | 7d | Backlog |

### Phase 3: Diagnosis

**Step 1 — Locate the affected code:**

```bash
# Find the module's source files
ls src/modules/<affected_module>/

# Find the API route if error_url points to an API
# Example: error on /api/noc/tickets → pages/api/noc/tickets.ts
find pages/api/ -name "*.ts" | grep <keyword>

# Find the page component if error_url points to a UI page
# Example: error on /projects/123 → pages/projects/[id]/index.tsx
find pages/ -name "*.tsx" | grep <keyword>
```

**Step 2 — Reproduce the error:**

Use the `steps_to_reproduce` from the ticket. If it's a UI issue, use browser automation:

```
1. mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp  (get browser context)
2. mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate          (go to error_url)
3. mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page         (get page state)
4. mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer          (follow reproduction steps)
```

**Step 3 — Analyze the stack trace:**

If `stack_trace` is provided, trace it through the codebase:

```bash
# Search for the error message in code
rg "ErrorMessage" src/ pages/

# Check the specific file:line from stack trace
# Read the file at that location
```

**Step 4 — Check logs:**

```bash
# Dev server logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i error

# Production logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i error

# Check for specific error patterns
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep "<ticket_keyword>"
```

**Step 5 — Database investigation:**

```sql
-- Check for data issues related to the ticket
-- Example: missing records, null values, constraint violations
SELECT * FROM <related_table> WHERE <condition> LIMIT 10;
```

### Phase 4: Fix Implementation

**Follow the PR workflow (MANDATORY):**

1. Create a feature branch: `fix/noc-<ticket_uid>-<short-description>`
2. Implement the fix
3. Run quality checks: `npm run lint && npm run type-check`
4. Run tests: `npm test`
5. Create PR via `/pr` skill
6. Update the ticket with PR link

**Update ticket status as you work:**

```sql
-- Mark ticket as in_progress when starting work
UPDATE maintenance_tickets SET status = 'in_progress' WHERE id = '<ticket_id>';

-- Update dev_ticket_details with branch/PR
UPDATE dev_ticket_details
SET github_branch = 'fix/noc-VF-XXXXXXXX-XXX-description',
    github_pr_url = 'https://github.com/VelocityFibre/FF_Next.js/pull/XXX',
    agent_status = 'running'
WHERE ticket_id = '<ticket_id>';
```

### Phase 5: Verification

DevOps tickets have 5 verification steps:

| Step | Name | Photo Required | Description |
|------|------|----------------|-------------|
| 1 | Issue Reproduction | Yes | Screenshot of the reproduced error |
| 2 | Root Cause Analysis | No | Document the root cause in notes |
| 3 | Fix Implementation | No | Link the PR, describe the fix |
| 4 | Testing & Verification | Yes | Screenshot of fix working in dev |
| 5 | Deployment | Yes | Screenshot of fix working in prod |

```bash
# Update verification step (example: step 2 - root cause)
curl -X PUT "http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets/<id>/verification/2" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "completed": true,
    "notes": "Root cause: missing null check in X component causing crash when Y is undefined"
  }'
```

## Common Patterns (Known Issues)

### Pattern: API returns `data.data` (double-wrapped response)
**Symptom:** UI shows blank/undefined values
**Cause:** `apiResponse.success(res, { success: true, data: {...} })` double-wraps
**Fix:** Remove inner wrapper — just pass the raw data to `apiResponse.success(res, data)`
**Ref:** Memory `MEMORY.md` — "apiResponse.success() Double-Wrapping Anti-Pattern"

### Pattern: Conditional SQL fragment breaks Neon
**Symptom:** SQL syntax error, query returns unexpected results
**Cause:** `${cond ? sql\`AND x\` : sql\`\`}` — template literal fragments don't compose in Neon
**Fix:** Use explicit query branches (if/else with full queries)
**Ref:** CLAUDE.md — "NO Conditional SQL Fragments"

### Pattern: Dynamic route params `undefined`
**Symptom:** API returns 404 or "invalid UUID"
**Cause:** Nested dynamic routes fail on Vercel, or inconsistent param names
**Fix:** Flatten routes (`contractors-stages.ts` not `[id]/stages.ts`), use consistent `[projectId]`

### Pattern: Numeric values are strings from Neon
**Symptom:** Math operations return NaN or concatenate instead of add
**Cause:** Neon returns numeric columns as strings
**Fix:** Always `Number()` before arithmetic

### Pattern: Missing `credentials: 'include'` in fetch
**Symptom:** 401 Unauthorized on API calls
**Cause:** Auth cookie not sent with request
**Fix:** Add `credentials: 'include'` to all fetch calls

### Pattern: `console.log` in production code
**Symptom:** Lint error or log noise
**Fix:** Replace with `import { log } from '@/lib/logger'` — use `log.info()`, `log.error()`, etc.

### Pattern: File > 300 lines
**Symptom:** Quality violation
**Fix:** Extract components/utilities into separate files

## Lessons Learned (Updated per ticket)

### 2026-03-13: VF-20260313-133 + VF-20260313-134
- **Schema column names differ from TypeScript types**: DB uses `type` not `ticket_type`, `status` not `ticket_status`. Always check actual schema with `\d maintenance_tickets` before querying.
- **psql connection**: Local psql defaults to port 5434 via socket. Use explicit: `PGPASSWORD=<pw> psql -h <host> -p 5432 -U neondb_owner -d neondb --set=sslmode=require`
- **z-index patterns**: ALL modals in codebase use `z-50` (not design tokens). Design system defines `--ff-z-modal-backdrop: 1040` and `--ff-z-modal: 1050` but they were never adopted. When fixing z-index, note this is a codebase-wide pattern, not a single-modal bug.
- **maintenance_notes schema**: Uses `created_by` (not `author_id`), has `is_resolution` boolean flag, `note_type` must be one of: internal, external, system.
- **Chrome DevTools scrolling**: Page content is in a `<main>` element that scrolls independently. Use `document.querySelector('main').scrollTop += N` via `evaluate_script`.
- **PR merge**: Branch protection requires `--admin` flag for gh merge. Auto-merge not enabled on repo.
- **Deploy workflow**: `sudo -u velo bash -c 'cd /home/velo/fibreflow-dev && git pull origin master && npm run build'` then `sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-dev.service`.

+ssh root@72.61.197.178 "tail -50 /opt/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.log | grep -E '(ACK RETRY|ACK FAILED|LOCAL ACK|ACK FALLBACK)'"

+# Health check cron log (runs every 5 minutes)

+Understanding which services depend on which helps prioritise during multi-service outages — fix the most upstream broken service first.
+├── CRITICAL: Neon PostgreSQL   (all API routes — no DB = 500 errors everywhere)
+├── IMPORTANT: VLM :8100        (Activate photo categorization, Fleet plate reads)
+├── IMPORTANT: WA Bridge :8083  (DR acknowledgments, WA feedback)

## Lessons Learned (Updated per ticket)

### 2026-03-13: VF-20260313-133 + VF-20260313-134
- **Schema column names differ from TypeScript types**: DB uses `type` not `ticket_type`, `status` not `ticket_status`. Always check actual schema with `\d maintenance_tickets` before querying.
- **psql connection**: Local psql defaults to port 5434 via socket. Use explicit: `PGPASSWORD=<pw> psql -h <host> -p 5432 -U neondb_owner -d neondb --set=sslmode=require`
- **z-index patterns**: ALL modals in codebase use `z-50` (not design tokens). Design system defines `--ff-z-modal-backdrop: 1040` and `--ff-z-modal: 1050` but they were never adopted. When fixing z-index, note this is a codebase-wide pattern, not a single-modal bug.
- **maintenance_notes schema**: Uses `created_by` (not `author_id`), has `is_resolution` boolean flag, `note_type` must be one of: internal, external, system.
- **Chrome DevTools scrolling**: Page content is in a `<main>` element that scrolls independently. Use `document.querySelector('main').scrollTop += N` via `evaluate_script`.
- **PR merge**: Branch protection requires `--admin` flag for gh merge. Auto-merge not enabled on repo.
- **Deploy workflow**: `sudo -u velo bash -c 'cd /home/velo/fibreflow-dev && git pull origin master && npm run build'` then `sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-dev.service`.

---

## Incident Runbooks

Step-by-step resolution procedures for the five most common FibreFlow incidents. Each runbook follows the Diagnose → Fix → Guard → Verify pattern.

---

### Runbook 1: 502 Bad Gateway (nginx → app not running)

**Symptom:** `https://app.fibreflow.app` or `https://dev.fibreflow.app` returns a 502 or shows the branded maintenance page.

**Health endpoints to check first:**
```bash
# Quick status — all environments
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/health | jq '.status'   # production
curl -s http://localhost:3005/api/health | jq '.status'   # dev

# Systemd service status
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-production.service
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-dev.service
```

**Step 1 — Identify which layer is broken:**
```bash
# Is the app process even listening?
ss -tlnp | grep -E '300[05]'

# Check nginx config (should be direct proxy_pass, no upstream blocks)
sudo nginx -t
grep -A3 'proxy_pass' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/vf-fibreflow

# Check systemd failure reason
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "30 min ago" | tail -50
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "30 min ago" | tail -50
```

**Step 2 — Check for crash-loop or build corruption:**
```bash
# Look for restart count (high = crash-loop)
sudo systemctl status fibreflow-production.service | grep -E '(Active|restarts)'

# Check if .next/BUILD_ID exists and is owned correctly
ls -la /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/BUILD_ID
stat /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/

# If .next is missing or owned by root, the build is corrupted
sudo ls /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next/ | head -5
```

**Step 3 — Standard recovery (try in order):**
```bash
# Option A: Simple restart (works for transient crashes)
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-production.service
sleep 10 && curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/health | jq '.status'

# Option B: Fix ownership + restart (works for mixed-user file issues)
sudo /usr/local/bin/fibreflow-fix-next /home/velo/fibreflow-production
sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-production.service

# Option C: Full redeploy (works for corrupted .next)
bash /home/hein/Workspace/FF_Next.js/scripts/deploy-local.sh production --force
```

**Step 4 — Verify nginx is not stuck on dead upstream:**
```bash
# Check current nginx config — should NOT have upstream blocks
grep -n 'upstream\|proxy_pass' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/vf-fibreflow

```bash
df -h
du -sh /home/velo/fibreflow-production/.next-backup-* 2>/dev/null | sort -h
# Remove old backups if disk is full (keep latest 3)
```

**Step 5 — GPU memory (VLM-specific):**
```bash
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free,utilization.gpu --format=csv
# If memory.used is near max and utilization is 0 = GPU memory leak
# Fix: restart vllm-qwen.service
```

**Step 6 — Scheduled maintenance (if nothing is actively crashing):**
The VLM service restarts nightly at 03:00 — this reclaims GPU memory. For Node.js, a weekly rolling restart is the safest approach; raise this with Hein if it becomes recurring.

**Escalate to Hein if:** OOM killer has terminated a service, disk usage is above 85%, or CPU stays above 95% for more than 10 minutes with no obvious cause.

---

## Log Analysis Commands

Reference commands for tailing and grepping service logs. Use these during Phase 3 (Diagnosis) of any ticket.

### Application Services (Velocity)

```bash
# Real-time log follow
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service -f
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service -f

# Last N lines
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service -n 100 --no-pager

# Time-bounded (ISO 8601 or relative)
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "2026-03-14 08:00:00"
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "1 hour ago"

# Error-only filter
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep -iE '(error|exception|fail|warn|unhandled|stack)'

# Specific module grep
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "30 min ago" | grep -i 'vlm\|activate\|procurement\|noc'

# API 5xx errors
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep -E '"status":(5[0-9]{2})'
```

### VLM Service (Velocity)

```bash
# Systemd journal (structured)
sudo journalctl -u vllm-qwen.service -n 50 --no-pager
sudo journalctl -u vllm-qwen.service --since "30 min ago" | grep -iE '(error|OOM|crash|timeout|CUDA)'

# VLM-specific log files
tail -100 /var/log/vllm-benchmark.log
tail -50 /var/log/vllm-maintenance.log

# Benchmark results (structured JSON)

### Escalate to Hein (do not attempt to resolve)

| Situation | Why | How to notify |
|-----------|-----|---------------|
| WA bridge requires QR code re-pair | Requires physical phone access | WhatsApp message to Hein directly |
| Production 502 lasting >15 minutes | SLA breach, customer impact | WhatsApp + update ticket as critical |
| Neon DB unreachable >15 minutes | Possible Neon platform incident | Check neonstatus.com, notify Hein |
| Database schema change needed | Requires migration review | Comment on ticket, do not apply |
| Production data corruption suspected | Risk of data loss | STOP all work on affected module |
| Auth/security vulnerability found | Credential leak, permission bypass | Direct message to Hein immediately |
| GPU failure or CUDA errors | Hardware level | Cannot fix in software |
| OpenClaw agent committed to deploy dir | `.next` corrupted by agent code | Check git reflog, notify Hein |
| Production deployment requested | Needs Hein approval | Post in ticket, wait for approval |
| Nginx config change required | Affects all environments | Submit PR, wait for Hein review |
| Service cost > $50 (Neon egress, etc.) | Budget impact | Flag in ticket |
| Unknown recurring crash (>5 restarts) | Root cause unclear | Escalate with full logs attached |

### Escalation message template

```
ESCALATION: [Ticket UID or "UNTICKETTED INCIDENT"]
TIME: [HH:MM SAST]
SEVERITY: [Critical / High / Medium]

SYMPTOM: [What the user/monitor observed]

[Paste relevant log lines here]

Send this via WhatsApp to Hein for critical incidents, and always update the ticket notes with the same content.

# /vlm — VLM Operations

Manages the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct Vision Language Model on Velocity. Used across multiple modules for photo categorization, data extraction, and QA validation.

## Quick Reference

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| **Service** | `vllm-qwen.service` |
| **Endpoint** | `http://100.96.203.105:8100` |
| **Model** | `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` |

| **Benchmark script** | `/home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmark.sh` |
| **Startup script** | `/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh` |

## Service Management (run locally on Velocity)

```bash
# Check status
sudo systemctl status vllm-qwen.service

# Full restart (preferred — uses startup script)
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh

# Emergency restart via systemd

# View live logs
sudo journalctl -u vllm-qwen.service -f

# View last 50 lines

## Health Check

```bash
# Quick health (from anywhere with Tailscale)
curl http://100.96.203.105:8100/health

# List loaded models (use this to verify model name)
curl http://100.96.203.105:8100/v1/models

# From FibreFlow API (checks same endpoint, returns JSON status)
curl https://dev.fibreflow.app/api/dr-dashboard/vlm-status

# Test simple inference
curl http://100.96.203.105:8100/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct",

/home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmark.sh

# View latest results
cat /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmarks/latest_results.json

### Expected Benchmark Results

| Test | Type | Expected Result | Target Time |

nvidia-smi

# GPU memory usage
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free,utilization.gpu --format=csv

# Expected: ~7-8GB used for model weights, plenty free
```

## Image Size Requirements

**CRITICAL:** Images exceeding 1024x768 cause token limit errors.

| Use Case | Max Dimensions |
|----------|---------------|
| DR Photos | 1024×768 |
| License Plates | 1024×768 |
| Fleet Odometers | 1024×768 |
| Documents / OCR | 1280×960 |

```typescript
// Resize before sending (use sharp)
import sharp from 'sharp';
const resized = await sharp(buffer)
  .resize(1024, 768, { fit: 'inside', withoutEnlargement: true })
  .jpeg({ quality: 85 })
  .toBuffer();
```

## VLM Configuration

Current stable settings (Jan 2026):
```
--model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
--max-model-len 16384
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
--dtype bfloat16
--max-num-seqs 4
--enforce-eager          # REQUIRED: prevents FLASHINFER crashes
```

**`--enforce-eager` is mandatory** — removing it causes CUDA kernel crashes.

## Scheduled Maintenance

| Schedule | Task |
|----------|------|
| 3:00 AM daily | VLM service restart (cron) |
| Every 5 min | Health check + auto-restart if down |
| 6am, 12pm, 6pm, 11pm | Benchmark runs (4× daily) |

---

## VLM Consumers in FibreFlow (All Modules)

Every module that calls the VLM at `:8100`. All use the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint.

| Module | Service File | Use Cases | Temperature | Timeout |
|--------|-------------|-----------|-------------|---------|
| **Activate — Categorization** | `src/modules/activate/services/categorizationVlmService.ts` | 10-step DR photo classification (House → Signature) | 0.1 | 3 min |
| **Activate — Extraction** | `src/modules/activate/services/vlmExtractionService.ts` | Power meter dBm (Step 7), ONT serial (Step 6 + 9), DR number (Step 9) | 0.1 | 3 min |
| **Activate — QA Validation** | `src/modules/activate/services/vlmQaValidationService.ts` | QA step validation scoring | 0.1 | varies |
| **Fleet** | `src/modules/fleet/services/fleetVlmService.ts` | Odometer OCR, license plate, fuel gauge level, fuel receipt, license disk | 0.1 | 1 min |
| **Assets** | `src/modules/assets/services/assetVlmService.ts` | Equipment label extraction: manufacturer, model, serial, MFG date, barcode | 0.1 | 1 min |
| **Construction QA** | `src/modules/construction-qa/services/vlmConstructionService.ts` | Civil/optical photo checklist step validation (8 civil steps) | 0.1 | varies |
| **Field Ops** | `src/modules/field-ops/services/fieldOpsVlmService.ts` | Pole photo civil/optical QA, pole number extraction + SOW cross-reference | 0.1 | varies |
| **Photo Review (legacy)** | `src/modules/photo-review/services/fotoVlmService.ts` | Deprecated — replaced by unifiedVlmService | — | — |

### API Routes That Trigger VLM

| Route | Trigger |
|-------|---------|
| `POST /api/cron/process-vlm-queue` | Every 5 min cron — processes up to 20 DRs (3 concurrent) |
| `POST /api/activate/process-wa-photo-vlm` | WhatsApp photo submission |
| `POST /api/fleet/check-in/process-vlm` | Fleet vehicle check-in |
| `POST /api/construction-qa/vlm-validate` | CQA review validation |

### Environment Variables Per Module

VLM_CATEGORIZATION_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct  # Activate categorization
VLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct      # Asset extraction

VLM_SERVICE_URL=http://100.96.203.105:8100            # Construction QA, Field Ops
```

---

## Categorization Accuracy Monitoring

### Check Current Accuracy via SQL

```sql
-- Overall accuracy by module (last 7 days)
SELECT
  module,
  analysis_type,
  SUM(total_extractions) AS total,
  SUM(correct_extractions) AS correct,
  SUM(corrected_extractions) AS corrected,
  ROUND(
    (SUM(correct_extractions) + SUM(corrected_extractions))::numeric
    / NULLIF(SUM(total_extractions), 0) * 100, 1
  ) AS accuracy_pct
FROM vlm_metrics
WHERE metric_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 days'
GROUP BY module, analysis_type
ORDER BY module, analysis_type;

-- Top error patterns (most common mistakes)
SELECT error_pattern, COUNT(*) AS occurrences
FROM vlm_corrections
WHERE created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
  AND error_pattern IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY error_pattern
ORDER BY occurrences DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- DR photo step confusion matrix (which steps are swapped)
SELECT
  vlm_extracted_value AS vlm_said,
  corrected_value AS correct_was,
  error_pattern,
  COUNT(*) AS times
FROM vlm_corrections
WHERE module = 'activate'
  AND analysis_type = 'construction_photo_qa'
  AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY times DESC;

-- Few-shot examples available (canonical ones injected into prompts)
SELECT module, analysis_type, COUNT(*) AS examples, SUM(is_canonical::int) AS canonical
FROM vlm_corrections
WHERE corrected_value IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY module, analysis_type
ORDER BY module;
```

### Run Accuracy Report via API

```bash
# Module accuracy summaries (last 7 days vs previous 7 days, with trend)

## Prompt Engineering Workflow

### Where Prompts Live

| Consumer | File | Prompt Location |
|----------|------|-----------------|
| DR photo step categorization | `categorizationVlmService.ts` | `buildCategorizationPrompt()` function |
| Power meter extraction | `vlmExtractionService.ts` | `POWER_METER_PROMPT` / `extractPowerMeter()` |
| ONT serial extraction (back) | `vlmExtractionService.ts` | `ONT_SERIAL_BACK_PROMPT` |
| ONT serial + DR number (front) | `vlmExtractionService.ts` | `STEP9_PROMPT` |
| Fleet odometer | `fleetVlmService.ts` | `ODOMETER_PROMPT` |
| Fleet license plate | `fleetVlmService.ts` | `LICENSE_PLATE_PROMPT` |
| Fleet fuel gauge | `fleetVlmService.ts` | `FUEL_GAUGE_PROMPT` |
| Asset label | `assetVlmService.ts` | `ASSET_LABEL_EXTRACTION_PROMPT` |
| CQA civil step | `vlmConstructionService.ts` | `buildCivilPrompt()` |
| Field ops civil | `fieldOpsVlmService.ts` | `CIVIL_PROMPT` |
| Field ops optical | `fieldOpsVlmService.ts` | `OPTICAL_PROMPT` |

### How to Modify a Prompt

1. **Read the current prompt** in the relevant service file.
2. **Check recent error patterns** in `vlm_corrections` to understand what the model gets wrong.
3. **Edit the prompt** — add `KEY DIFFERENTIATORS` sections for confused pairs (see the 10-step prompt in `categorizationVlmService.ts` as a reference pattern).
4. **Do NOT change** `VLM_TEMPERATURE` (keep at 0.1 for consistency) or `max_tokens` without understanding token budget.
5. **Test via dry-run** using the retest workflow above.
6. **Monitor accuracy** by watching `vlm_metrics` for a day after deployment.

### Few-Shot Learning (HITL)

The system automatically injects human-correction examples into prompts at runtime:

- **Source table:** `vlm_corrections` — every time a human overrides a VLM result, it's recorded here.
- **Canonical examples:** Mark high-quality corrections as canonical via `markAsCanonical(id, true)` — these are prioritized in prompt injection.
- **Automatic injection:** `categorizationVlmService.ts` calls `getRelevantExamples()` before every batch. Up to 5 examples are appended to the prompt.
- **Control injection:** Set `maxExamples` in `getRelevantExamples()` options (default: 5). Set to 0 to disable temporarily.

```sql
-- Mark a correction as canonical (high priority for prompt injection)
UPDATE vlm_corrections SET is_canonical = TRUE, priority = 10
WHERE id = '<correction-uuid>';

-- See what few-shot examples the model is currently seeing for DR photos
SELECT id, vlm_extracted_value, corrected_value, correction_notes, is_canonical, priority
FROM vlm_corrections
WHERE module = 'activate' AND analysis_type = 'construction_photo_qa'
ORDER BY is_canonical DESC, priority DESC, created_at DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### Prompt Testing with Binary Queries (CQA Scripts)

For construction QA, the Python scripts use a **binary YES/NO** pattern — more reliable than multi-class for hard-to-distinguish steps:

```python
# Pattern from reclassify-targeted.py
# Ask "Does this photo show X?" instead of "Which of these 8 steps is this?"
# Confidence threshold: 0.8 for targeted, 0.7 for few-shot
```

Use this binary pattern when accuracy on a specific step is below ~75%.

## Troubleshooting

### Service Not Responding (run locally on Velocity)
```bash
nvidia-smi                          # 1. Check GPU is visible
sudo systemctl status vllm-qwen.service  # 2. Check service state
sudo journalctl -u vllm-qwen.service -n 50  # 3. Check errors
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh  # 4. Clean restart
```

### Token Limit Error (HTTP 400)
- **Symptom:** `"decoder prompt is longer than maximum model length"`
- **Cause:** Image is too large
- **Fix:** Resize to max 1024×768 before sending

### VLM Returns Garbage Output
- **Likely cause:** Prompt format issue
- **Check:** `vlmExtractionService.ts` prompt structure
- **Test:** Run benchmark to verify model is healthy

### GPU OOM (Out of Memory)
```bash
# Check what's using GPU memory
nvidia-smi
# Kill any orphaned processes if needed
# Then restart VLM service
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh
```

### FLASHINFER Crashes
- **Fix:** Ensure `--enforce-eager` is in service config
- Check `/etc/systemd/system/vllm-qwen.service` for the flag

### Categorization Consistently Wrong for One Step

1. Query `vlm_corrections` for that step's error pattern.
2. Add a `KEY DIFFERENTIATORS` bullet in `buildCategorizationPrompt()`.
3. Run `reclassify-targeted.py --dry-run` to verify improvement.
4. Check that the few-shot learning table has corrections for that step.

### Fleet VLM Getting Wrong Odometer Readings

The most common odometer error patterns are `digit_1_7`, `digit_6_8`, `digit_8_0`. Each is tracked in `vlm_corrections.error_pattern`. If a pattern recurs:

1. Record the correction via the fleet check-in UI (auto-populates `vlm_corrections`).
2. Check if the correction is marked canonical: `SELECT is_canonical FROM vlm_corrections WHERE id = '...'`.
3. Mark it canonical if it is a clear, unambiguous example.
4. The next fleet VLM call will have this injected as a few-shot hint.

## Model Upgrade Procedure

Follow these steps to safely swap Qwen3-VL-8B for a newer model (e.g., Qwen3-VL-72B or a fine-tuned variant).

### Pre-upgrade Checklist

1. **Record a baseline:** Run the full benchmark suite and save results.
   ```bash
   /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmark.sh
   cp /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmarks/latest_results.json \
      /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmarks/pre_upgrade_baseline.json
   ```

2. **Snapshot VLM metrics DB:**
   ```sql
   -- Save current accuracy baseline
   SELECT module, analysis_type,
     ROUND(SUM(correct_extractions + corrected_extractions)::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(total_extractions), 0) * 100, 1) AS accuracy_pct
   FROM vlm_metrics
   WHERE metric_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '14 days'
   GROUP BY module, analysis_type;
   ```

3. **Identify all places that hard-code the model name:**
   - `categorizationVlmService.ts` — `VLM_CATEGORIZATION_MODEL` env var (or fallback string)
   - `vlmExtractionService.ts` — model name in request body
   - `fleetVlmService.ts` — `FLEET_VLM_MODEL` env var
   - `assetVlmService.ts` — `VLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL` env var
   - `fieldOpsVlmService.ts` — `VLM_MODEL` constant
   - `vlmConstructionService.ts` — `VLM_MODEL` constant
   - Python scripts — `VLM_MODEL` at top of each script

4. **Check GPU memory headroom** — larger models need more VRAM:
   ```bash
   nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.free --format=csv
   ```

### Upgrade Steps

```bash
# 1. Download new model (in vLLM-accessible location)
#    Usually done via huggingface-cli or vLLM's model caching
huggingface-cli download Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL

# 2. Edit the service file
sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/vllm-qwen.service
# Change: --model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
# To:     --model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL
# Adjust: --gpu-memory-utilization if model is larger

# 3. Reload systemd and restart
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh

# 4. Wait for model to load (watch logs — takes 1-3 minutes)
sudo journalctl -u vllm-qwen.service -f

# 5. Verify model is loaded
curl http://100.96.203.105:8100/v1/models

# 6. Run benchmark suite against new model
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmark.sh

# 7. Compare with baseline
diff /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmarks/pre_upgrade_baseline.json \
     /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmarks/latest_results.json
```

### Update Model References in Code

After confirming the new model works:

```bash
# Update env vars in .env.local (dev and production)
# VLM_CATEGORIZATION_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL
# FLEET_VLM_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL
# VLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL

# Update hard-coded model references in Python scripts
sed -i 's|Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct|Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL|g' \
  scripts/classify-qa-photos-vlm.py \
  scripts/reclassify-targeted.py \
  scripts/reclassify-fewshot.py \
  scripts/reclassify-optical.py
```

### Rollback

```bash

sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/vllm-qwen.service
# Revert --model line

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh
```

The `vlmLearningService.ts` (`src/services/vlmLearningService.ts`) provides enterprise-wide correction tracking and few-shot example management.

### Database Tables

| Table | Purpose |
|-------|---------|

### Analysis Types Tracked

`ont_serial_back`, `ont_serial_front`, `power_meter_dbm`, `dr_number`, `license_plate`, `odometer`, `fuel_gauge`, `fuel_receipt`, `license_disk`, `construction_photo_qa`, `equipment_label`

### Error Patterns Automatically Classified

The system auto-classifies error patterns when a correction is recorded:

- `digit_1_7`, `digit_1_6`, `digit_6_8`, `digit_8_0`, `digit_9_4`, `digit_2_3` — digit confusion
- `ssid_not_serial`, `part_number_not_serial`, `mac_not_serial` — field confusion (ONT serials)
- `step_classified_unrelated`, `step_2_overassigned`, `step_N_to_M` — categorization errors
- `trip_not_odometer` — fleet odometer
- `gauge_reversed` — fuel gauge
- `missed_decimal`, `extra_decimal` — format errors
- `length_mismatch`, `totally_wrong` — general mismatches

## Categorization Accuracy Monitoring

### Check Current Accuracy via SQL

```sql
-- Overall accuracy by module (last 7 days)
SELECT
  module,
  analysis_type,
  SUM(total_extractions) AS total,
  SUM(correct_extractions) AS correct,
  SUM(corrected_extractions) AS corrected,
  ROUND(
    (SUM(correct_extractions) + SUM(corrected_extractions))::numeric
    / NULLIF(SUM(total_extractions), 0) * 100, 1
  ) AS accuracy_pct
FROM vlm_metrics
WHERE metric_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 days'
GROUP BY module, analysis_type
ORDER BY module, analysis_type;

-- Top error patterns (most common mistakes)
SELECT error_pattern, COUNT(*) AS occurrences
FROM vlm_corrections
WHERE created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
  AND error_pattern IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY error_pattern
ORDER BY occurrences DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- DR photo step confusion matrix (which steps are swapped)
SELECT
  vlm_extracted_value AS vlm_said,
  corrected_value AS correct_was,
  error_pattern,
  COUNT(*) AS times
FROM vlm_corrections
WHERE module = 'activate'
  AND analysis_type = 'construction_photo_qa'
  AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY times DESC;

-- Few-shot examples available (canonical ones injected into prompts)

## Prompt Engineering Workflow

### Where Prompts Live

| Consumer | File | Prompt Location |
|----------|------|-----------------|
| DR photo step categorization | `categorizationVlmService.ts` | `buildCategorizationPrompt()` function |
| Power meter extraction | `vlmExtractionService.ts` | `POWER_METER_PROMPT` / `extractPowerMeter()` |
| ONT serial extraction (back) | `vlmExtractionService.ts` | `ONT_SERIAL_BACK_PROMPT` |
| ONT serial + DR number (front) | `vlmExtractionService.ts` | `STEP9_PROMPT` |
| Fleet odometer | `fleetVlmService.ts` | `ODOMETER_PROMPT` |
| Fleet license plate | `fleetVlmService.ts` | `LICENSE_PLATE_PROMPT` |
| Fleet fuel gauge | `fleetVlmService.ts` | `FUEL_GAUGE_PROMPT` |
| Asset label | `assetVlmService.ts` | `ASSET_LABEL_EXTRACTION_PROMPT` |
| CQA civil step | `vlmConstructionService.ts` | `buildCivilPrompt()` |
| Field ops civil | `fieldOpsVlmService.ts` | `CIVIL_PROMPT` |
| Field ops optical | `fieldOpsVlmService.ts` | `OPTICAL_PROMPT` |

### How to Modify a Prompt

1. **Read the current prompt** in the relevant service file.
2. **Check recent error patterns** in `vlm_corrections` to understand what the model gets wrong.
3. **Edit the prompt** — add `KEY DIFFERENTIATORS` sections for confused pairs (see the 10-step prompt in `categorizationVlmService.ts` as a reference pattern).
4. **Do NOT change** `VLM_TEMPERATURE` (keep at 0.1 for consistency) or `max_tokens` without understanding token budget.
5. **Test via dry-run** using the retest workflow above.
6. **Monitor accuracy** by watching `vlm_metrics` for a day after deployment.

### Few-Shot Learning (HITL)

The system automatically injects human-correction examples into prompts at runtime:

- **Source table:** `vlm_corrections` — every time a human overrides a VLM result, it's recorded here.
- **Canonical examples:** Mark high-quality corrections as canonical via `markAsCanonical(id, true)` — these are prioritized in prompt injection.
- **Automatic injection:** `categorizationVlmService.ts` calls `getRelevantExamples()` before every batch. Up to 5 examples are appended to the prompt.
- **Control injection:** Set `maxExamples` in `getRelevantExamples()` options (default: 5). Set to 0 to disable temporarily.

```sql
-- Mark a correction as canonical (high priority for prompt injection)
UPDATE vlm_corrections SET is_canonical = TRUE, priority = 10
WHERE id = '<correction-uuid>';

-- See what few-shot examples the model is currently seeing for DR photos
SELECT id, vlm_extracted_value, corrected_value, correction_notes, is_canonical, priority
FROM vlm_corrections
WHERE module = 'activate' AND analysis_type = 'construction_photo_qa'
ORDER BY is_canonical DESC, priority DESC, created_at DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### Prompt Testing with Binary Queries (CQA Scripts)

For construction QA, the Python scripts use a **binary YES/NO** pattern — more reliable than multi-class for hard-to-distinguish steps:

```python
# Pattern from reclassify-targeted.py
# Ask "Does this photo show X?" instead of "Which of these 8 steps is this?"
# Confidence threshold: 0.8 for targeted, 0.7 for few-shot
```

Use this binary pattern when accuracy on a specific step is below ~75%.

## Troubleshooting

### Service Not Responding (run locally on Velocity)
```bash
nvidia-smi                          # 1. Check GPU is visible
sudo systemctl status vllm-qwen.service  # 2. Check service state
sudo journalctl -u vllm-qwen.service -n 50  # 3. Check errors
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh  # 4. Clean restart
```

### Token Limit Error (HTTP 400)
- **Symptom:** `"decoder prompt is longer than maximum model length"`
- **Cause:** Image is too large
- **Fix:** Resize to max 1024×768 before sending

### VLM Returns Garbage Output
- **Likely cause:** Prompt format issue
- **Check:** `vlmExtractionService.ts` prompt structure
- **Test:** Run benchmark to verify model is healthy

### GPU OOM (Out of Memory)
```bash
# Check what's using GPU memory
nvidia-smi
# Kill any orphaned processes if needed
# Then restart VLM service
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh
```

### FLASHINFER Crashes
- **Fix:** Ensure `--enforce-eager` is in service config
- Check `/etc/systemd/system/vllm-qwen.service` for the flag

### Categorization Consistently Wrong for One Step

1. Query `vlm_corrections` for that step's error pattern.
2. Add a `KEY DIFFERENTIATORS` bullet in `buildCategorizationPrompt()`.
3. Run `reclassify-targeted.py --dry-run` to verify improvement.
4. Check that the few-shot learning table has corrections for that step.

### Fleet VLM Getting Wrong Odometer Readings

The most common odometer error patterns are `digit_1_7`, `digit_6_8`, `digit_8_0`. Each is tracked in `vlm_corrections.error_pattern`. If a pattern recurs:

1. Record the correction via the fleet check-in UI (auto-populates `vlm_corrections`).
2. Check if the correction is marked canonical: `SELECT is_canonical FROM vlm_corrections WHERE id = '...'`.
3. Mark it canonical if it is a clear, unambiguous example.
4. The next fleet VLM call will have this injected as a few-shot hint.

## Model Upgrade Procedure

Follow these steps to safely swap Qwen3-VL-8B for a newer model (e.g., Qwen3-VL-72B or a fine-tuned variant).

### Pre-upgrade Checklist

1. **Record a baseline:** Run the full benchmark suite and save results.
   ```bash
   /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmark.sh
   cp /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmarks/latest_results.json \
      /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmarks/pre_upgrade_baseline.json
   ```

2. **Snapshot VLM metrics DB:**
   ```sql
   -- Save current accuracy baseline
   SELECT module, analysis_type,
     ROUND(SUM(correct_extractions + corrected_extractions)::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(total_extractions), 0) * 100, 1) AS accuracy_pct
   FROM vlm_metrics
   WHERE metric_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '14 days'
   GROUP BY module, analysis_type;
   ```

3. **Identify all places that hard-code the model name:**
   - `categorizationVlmService.ts` — `VLM_CATEGORIZATION_MODEL` env var (or fallback string)
   - `vlmExtractionService.ts` — model name in request body
   - `fleetVlmService.ts` — `FLEET_VLM_MODEL` env var
   - `assetVlmService.ts` — `VLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL` env var
   - `fieldOpsVlmService.ts` — `VLM_MODEL` constant
   - `vlmConstructionService.ts` — `VLM_MODEL` constant
   - Python scripts — `VLM_MODEL` at top of each script

4. **Check GPU memory headroom** — larger models need more VRAM:
   ```bash
   nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.free --format=csv
   ```

### Upgrade Steps

```bash
# 1. Download new model (in vLLM-accessible location)
#    Usually done via huggingface-cli or vLLM's model caching
huggingface-cli download Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL

# 2. Edit the service file
sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/vllm-qwen.service
# Change: --model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
# To:     --model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL
# Adjust: --gpu-memory-utilization if model is larger

# 3. Reload systemd and restart
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh

# 4. Wait for model to load (watch logs — takes 1-3 minutes)
sudo journalctl -u vllm-qwen.service -f

# 5. Verify model is loaded
curl http://100.96.203.105:8100/v1/models

# 6. Run benchmark suite against new model
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmark.sh

# 7. Compare with baseline
diff /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmarks/pre_upgrade_baseline.json \
     /home/velo/scripts/vllm/benchmarks/latest_results.json
```

### Update Model References in Code

After confirming the new model works:

```bash
# Update env vars in .env.local (dev and production)
# VLM_CATEGORIZATION_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL
# FLEET_VLM_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL
# VLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL

# Update hard-coded model references in Python scripts
sed -i 's|Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct|Qwen/Qwen3-VL-NEW-MODEL|g' \
  scripts/classify-qa-photos-vlm.py \
  scripts/reclassify-targeted.py \
  scripts/reclassify-fewshot.py \
  scripts/reclassify-optical.py
```

### Rollback

```bash
# Edit service to restore old model
sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/vllm-qwen.service
# Revert --model line

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
/home/velo/scripts/vllm/startup.sh
```

The `vlmLearningService.ts` tracks prompt versions via SHA-256 hash. After changing a prompt, the hash changes automatically when the next extraction runs. To verify the new prompt hash is being used:

FROM vlm_corrections
WHERE module = 'activate'
